extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering dataset consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. Annotators are presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results, and annotate a long answer (typically a paragraph) and a short answer (one or more entities) if present on the page, or marks null if no long/short answer is present.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were sampled from Google search engine queries of 8 words or more that had been issued by multiple users in a short period of time. These questions were then paired with Wikipedia pages, and annotators provided long answers (bounding boxes containing relevant information) and short answers (entities or yes/no responses) for each question-page pair.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of Google search engine queries (8 words or more issued by multiple users in a short period) and Wikipedia pages. The dataset contains (question, wikipedia page, long answer, short answer) quadruples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation performed using custom annotation interface by pool of around 50 annotators, with average annotation time of 80 seconds. Guidelines and tooling divide the annotation process.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality evaluated using two methods: 1) post hoc evaluation of correctness of non-null answers under consensus judgments from four 'experts'; 2) k-way annotations (with k = 25) on a subset of the data. Post hoc evaluation measures annotation precision, while 25-way annotated data provide insights into recall when combined with expert judgments.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 25 annotations per item for a subset of the data
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses on longer queries (8 words or more) and Wikipedia as the primary source of factual information. Questions beginning with 'how to' are excluded. The choice of Wikipedia as the sole source may introduce stylistic biases similar to other factual information sources on the Web.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to questions of 8 words or more, excludes 'how to' questions, and is restricted to Wikipedia documents. Future data collection efforts may need to introduce shorter queries, 'how to' questions, or domains other than Wikipedia. There is genuine ambiguity in whether answers are acceptable for naturally occurring questions, and often multiple acceptable answers exist.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, development, and testing of question answering systems. The public release contains 307,373 training examples with single annotations, 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data, and 7,842 5-way annotated items sequestered as test data. The task is designed to be close to an end-to-end question answering application.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions are filtered using heuristics to select fact-seeking queries of 8+ words from Google search logs. Queries are run through Google search engine and retained only if a Wikipedia page appears in top 5 results. Questions are categorized as 'good' (fact-seeking, answerable with entity/explanation) or 'bad' (ambiguous, incomprehensible, opinion-seeking, etc.).
